short.cost_scope: Hidden/history capture clones, defensive five-tensor history hit copies, whole-source guards, fresh prompt equality, live complete-head replay and per-group cleanup execute inside native complete-update timers. Worker-wide guard_seconds includes history checks; capture_seconds measures hidden-input capture only, not history-clone time. Cleanup is worker-wide. These host accumulators include warmup, are not GPU durations, and cannot be added or subtracted to infer gains. History clone byte counters include admission and hit copies. Per-group entry/exit are timed; persistent decoder setup/cleanup are outside and separate. No diagnostic timings are included.
limits: One fresh process per arm; paired positions share seeds/workloads, not randomized repeated trials or a reference/reference noise estimate.

Both arms use the identical production benchmark/group/policy implementation, with no hotpath runtime patches; only the configured history-encoder toggle differs; both arms retain hidden replay and decoder staging.
Owned hidden/prompt/history payload bytes, including pending history and defensive hit copies, are distinct from allocator reservation, peak CUDA allocation changes and bounded host key metadata.

The production factory asserts empty owned cache after successful group replay; zero weakref observations do not prove allocator release or absent storage aliases. Native exceptions may retain borrowed tensor objects in tracebacks while cache ownership is dropped.

qualification.cpu_source_boundary: Focused CPU runs occurred during finalization. Five initial Gloo socket permission failures passed isolated retries with local socket access and CUDA hidden. Two compacted-encoder policy cases require CUDA and were skipped; one policy case was deselected. The pinned final source separately passed CUDA and CLI qualification embedded in each pair.
qualification.cli_scope: Real RustBPE, checkpoint/re-exec, fork, evaluation and uninterrupted training with history enabled. The CLI checks settings and cleanup, but does not independently require history hits; the generated depth-2 CUDA fixture requires nonvacuous hits and exact three-update parity.

limitations: One RTX 4090, one fresh process per arm/workload, five short and three full measured updates. No randomized campaign, reference/reference noise estimate or confidence interval.
Linear-head production timing; separate depth-2 CUDA and CLI correctness qualification supplies no depth-2 production throughput claim.
Worker counters include warmup. Timing comparisons use measured updates only. Host guard/capture accumulators cannot be subtracted from synchronized timings.
Owned tensor payload, peak CUDA allocation and allocator reservations are distinct measures; separate peaks need not occur together.
No full-suite, Hopper, distributed/full-policy acceleration or natural OOM recovery qualification.
One-second compute PID observations cannot exclude subsecond processes, graphics work or CPU contention.
Earlier instrumented equality/cost diagnostics establish feasibility only; their durations do not enter these performance results.
